7.1 Overview of Yard Logistics
The yard logistics process involves a number of steps, including the following:
Receiving goods
The process typically starts with the receipt of goods into the yard. This step
can involve checking the goods against the shipping manifest, ensuring that
the correct quantities and items have been received, and organizing the
goods for storage or further distribution.
Storage and retrieval
Once the goods have been received, they must be stored within the yard. This
step involves finding an appropriate location within the yard to store the
goods and ensuring that they are stored safely and securely. When the goods
are needed for distribution or transportation, they must be retrieved from
storage.
Inventory management
Effective yard logistics also requires careful inventory management. This step
involves keeping track of the quantities and locations of items within the
yard, as well as monitoring the flow of goods in and out of the yard to ensure
that inventory levels are maintained.
Equipment and personnel management
Yard logistics also involves managing the equipment and personnel needed
to move goods within the yard. This step can include coordinating the use of
forklifts, pallet jacks, and other handling equipment, as well as managing
personnel schedules and ensuring that workers are trained and equipped to
carry out their duties safely and efficiently.
Transportation management
Finally, yard logistics also involves coordinating the movement of goods into
and out of the yard. This step can include scheduling deliveries and pickups,
coordinating with transportation providers, and ensuring that goods are
transported in a timely and efficient manner.
Businesses across various sectors and industries, engaged in the movement of
goods through logistics and supply, have come to acknowledge that
transportation disruptions frequently occur not just on the road, but also when
resources are situated in the yards of your manufacturing plants and distribution
centers.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

420
Effective yard logistics requires careful planning, coordination, and execution of
these processes in order to ensure that goods are moved through the supply
chain in a safe, efficient, and cost-effective manner. The efficiency of modern
manufacturing operations and warehouses can be hampered by various
inefficiencies in their yards, such as the following:
Inadequate visibility into shipments and trailers, making it difficult to shuttle
them between plants and distribution centers.
The availability of space is a major challenge for yard management,
particularly in urban areas where land is scarce and expensive. Limited space
can make it difficult to accommodate large numbers of vehicles and
shipments and can also impact the speed and efficiency of operations.
Shipping delays for inbound and outbound goods.
Poor management of yard trailers, leading to higher expenses on spotters and
shuttles.
Challenges in locating empty trailers to meet outbound load schedules.
Delayed truck driver pickups.
Traffic congestion is another common challenge in yard management,
particularly in busy transportation hubs such as ports and airports.
Congestion, particularly at entry and exit gates, can slow down operations,
increase waiting times for drivers, and result in delays and increased costs.
Effective communication is crucial in yard management, particularly when
coordinating activities with carriers, drivers, and other stakeholders. Poor
communication can lead to misunderstandings, delays, and safety issues.
Insufficient visibility into the arrival of shipments at destination facilities.
Yard management also involves ensuring the safety and security of personnel,
equipment, and shipments. This goal can be challenging, particularly in high-
traffic areas where there is a risk of accident, theft, and damage. You may
have limited ability to monitor safety and compliance violations.
Many yard management operations are still reliant on manual processes and
paper-based systems, which can be time consuming and prone to errors.
Integrating technology such as radio frequency identification (RFID) and GPS
can help streamline operations and improve visibility, but integrating these
technologies can also be a complex and costly process.
© 

421
Extreme weather conditions, such as snow, rain, and wind, can impact yard
operations and cause delays and safety issues. Preparing for and managing
these conditions requires careful planning and coordination.
To remain competitive in global markets, companies with yards must implement
professional logistics processes that are supported by a highly integrated and
user-friendly system across the entire supply chain. The use of SAP Yard Logistics
can provide comprehensive support for transportation units (TUs) from check-in
to check-out, with a focus on planning, execution, yard operations, monitoring,
and billing functionalities. SAP Yard Logistics serves as the crucial link that
connects transportation management, extended warehouse management
(EWM), and SAP ERP.
To successfully complete yard processes, several key features of SAP Yard
Logistics are essential, including the following:
Seamless integration with SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM) and SAP
EWM
Proper classification of TUs
SAP Dock Appointment Scheduling
Efficient task planning
Cross-docking capabilities
Accurate location determination
Mobile yard execution for flexibility and mobility
Integration with SAP Environment, Health, and Safety Management (SAP EHS
Management)
Proper classification of TUs
Effective exception handling
Comprehensive checking and measuring of activities
Mobile yard execution for flexibility and mobility
Streamlined internal yard processes
Real-time monitoring and alerting
Easy printing of relevant documents
Convenient driver self-service check-in

422
Effective exception handling
Internet of Things (IoT) enablement and integration capabilities
Easy printing of relevant document
Accurate billing of yard tasks
SAP Yard Logistics is a powerful tool that effectively manages, controls, and
streamlines transport processes and vehicle movements within the plant
premises, commonly known as the yard. Through its advanced 2D and 3D
graphical layouts, SAP Yard Logistics enables real-time monitoring and
visualization of the current situation on site, providing complete transparency at
all times with regards to all goods-moving and transport-relevant processes in
the yard
By integrating SAP Yard Logistics into other SAP solutions such as SAP EWM, SAP
TM, and SAP Business Network for Logistics, manual processes can be
eliminated, leading to the optimization of logistics processes. This integration
results in enhanced efficiency, reduced errors, and improved customer
satisfaction.
As shown in Figure 7.1, SAP Yard Logistics offers several benefits, including the
following:
SAP Yard Logistics provides maximum transparency when it comes to yard
processes, resulting in improved efficiency and productivity. It significantly
reduces check-in and check-out times and optimizes the use of assets and
yard areas. Through tracking functions, it reduces truck waiting times, and by
monitoring and alerting, it identifies bottlenecks in the process.
SAP Yard Logistics also offers cross-docking functions for combined delivery
and collection, which increases efficiency and reduces costs. The solution can
track and trace vehicles as well as swap bodies, trailers, and containers within
a yard, which leads to greater control and management of resources. With its
advanced yard automation features, such as scoreboards, RFID, and GPS, it
enables IoT scenarios and provides greater visibility into yard operations.
Planning yard activities is a fundamental basis for yard automation, and SAP
Yard Logistics streamlines this process by automating tasks and integrating
with other SAP solutions such as SAP EWM and SAP TM. In this way, it
optimizes yard operations, reduces errors, and improves customer
satisfaction.
© 

423
Figure 7.1 SAP Yard Logistics Overview
SAP Yard Logistics is available in two versions to suit different organizational
needs:
Add-on for SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management
The first variant is as an add-on for SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management,
which provides organizations with a comprehensive solution for managing
their yard logistics operations. The add-on is fully integrated with SAP
S/4HANA and provides users with real-time visibility into all yard activities to
optimize yard operations.
Standalone SAP S/4HANA application
The second variant is a standalone SAP S/4HANA application that can be
connected to either an SAP S/4HANA Enterprise Management or a legacy
enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. This option allows organizations
to use SAP Yard Logistics as a standalone solution, enabling them to manage
their yard logistics operations separately from their other ERP processes.
Both variants of SAP Yard Logistics as shown in Figure 7.2 provide organizations
with a range of features and capabilities, including real-time visibility into yard
operations, advanced planning and scheduling, automated processes, and
enhanced collaboration among all stakeholders. Organizations can choose the
variant that best suits their specific requirements and business processes.
Figure 7.2 SAP Yard Logistics Deployments

SAP Yard Logistics and SAP EWM are two separate SAP solutions that can be

following the integration options between SAP Yard Logistics and SAP EWM are
available:
SAP Yard Logistics can be integrated with SAP EWM to create inbound and
outbound deliveries for managing goods receipt and goods issue processes.
This integration allows for the seamless transfer of data between the two
systems and ensures that all warehouse movements are tracked and
managed efficiently.
In addition to supporting planning and operational processes, SAP Yard
Logistics facilitates integration scenarios (using sample integration
functionality) in conjunction with either SAP ERP, SAP TM, or SAP EWM.
In conclusion, integrating SAP Yard Logistics and SAP EWM can provide
organizations with a comprehensive and efficient WMS that can streamline their
operations and improve their supply chain performance.

7.2 Using SAP Yard Logistics
In this section, we’ll provide a detailed explanation of SAP Yard Logistics. We’ll
begin with the inbound process and cover the outbound process as well. For
both scenarios, we’ll walk through the business process, configuration, and
master data setup needed then provide a process demonstration.
7.2.1 Inbound Process
The purpose of the inbound logistics process with SAP Yard Logistics is to
streamline the flow of goods and materials into a company’s operations,
ensuring efficient operations, reducing costs, and enhancing customer
satisfaction. We’ll look at the inbound process in detail in the following sections.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 7.3, the inbound process using SAP Yard Logistics involves
the following steps:
1. The first step in the inbound goods process is to create a purchase order for
a vendor in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. The purchase order is then converted
to an inbound delivery, which is automatically distributed to SAP EWM for
warehouse processing.
2. Once the planning is complete, the shipment is distributed to SAP EWM as
well as SAP Yard Logistics to trigger the process of truck arrival, loading, and
departure. The message from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA triggers the creation
of the yard request in SAP Yard Logistics, which is used to plan the first yard
activity.
3. At the same time, the message from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is also sent to
SAP EWM, a dependent document is created, namely the TU, which contains
information about the planned content. In addition, an automatic door
determination or manual door assignment occurs, allowing SAP EWM to
begin the putaway and staging process. Note that, since SAP EWM and SAP
Yard Logistics are involved in this process, no yard activities, such as check-
in postings or movements, will be executed. These steps fall within the
scope of SAP Yard Logistics.
© 

427
Figure 7.3 Inbound Process Using SAP Yard Logistics
4. While the warehouse begins its activities in SAP Yard Logistics, the yard
order is created based on the yard request, which is used for processing in
the yard. In an inbound scenario such as this, an inbound yard order will be
created. For the departure of the truck, an outbound yard order is required,
which can be generated from the inbound yard order.
5. Meanwhile, in SAP EWM, the inbound process is performed, and the
products are unloaded and putaway. At the same time, different yard
activities are taking place in SAP Yard Logistics. Once the movement to the
door is activated, another door determination may occur. This step is used
when no door determination was triggered earlier or to validate the
previously determined door.
6. With confirmation of the yard task in SAP Yard Logistics, the arrival at the
door will be posted in SAP EWM. At this point, the TU can no longer be
moved in the yard. Activities in the yard will only be possible again after
receiving notification from SAP EWM that the unloading has been
completed.
7. This notification triggers yard operations to start the movement from the
door to the next yard location, such as the checkpoint for departure. A
message about this pending departure from the door is sent from SAP Yard
Logistics to SAP EWM. Meanwhile, the goods receipt can be triggered in SAP
EWM. The latest point for a goods receipt posting is during the check-out of
the TU. Again, after the unloading notification has been sent to SAP Yard
Logistics, no further yard activities are allowed in SAP EWM. All postings
happen in SAP Yard Logistics.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

428
8. Now that the truck has reached the inbound checkpoint, the check-in can
be posted. This check-in will also be sent to SAP EWM, triggering the check-
in posting there. Based on the goods receipt and check-in posting in SAP
EWM, SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA documents will be updated.
Configuration
In this section, we’ll cover the key configuration required for this process,
assuming that the basic configuration in SAP EWM, SAP ERP, or SAP S/4HANA,
and SAP Yard Logistics have already been performed in the system:
1. Assign SAP EWM business systems and warehouses to yard in SAP Yard
Logistics
This configuration setting is required to integrate SAP Yard Logistics with
SAP EWM. Follow the IMG menu path Yard Logistics • Integration •
Integration to SAP Extended Warehouse Management • Assign SAP EWM
Business Systems and Warehouses to Yard. Click New Entries and
maintain the entry or entries or verify that these settings meet your
business requirements, as shown in Figure 7.4.
Figure 7.4 Assign SAP EWM Business Systems and Warehouses to Yards
2. Maintain SAP EWM checkpoints in SAP Yard Logistics
This configuration setting is to maintain checkpoints. Follow the IMG menu
path Yard Logistics • Integration • Integration to SAP Extended
Warehouse Management • Maintain EWM Checkpoints. Click New Entries
and maintain the entry or verify that these settings meet your business
requirements, as shown in Figure 7.5.
© 

429
Figure 7.5 Maintain SAP EWM Checkpoints
Master Data Setup
Let’s delve into the master data setup required for an inbound goods receipt
process using SAP Yard Logistics, which involves the following:
1. Link between packaging material (for the TU) and means of transport in
SAP Yard Logistics
In this master data setup, you’ll use the SAP Fiori app Link Between
Packaging Material (TU) and Means of Transport. In this app, maintain link
for various means of transport (MTr) and packaging material (Packaging
Material) as shown in Figure 7.6.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

430
Figure 7.6 Link between Packaging Material (TU) and Means of Transport
2. Assign a docking location to a warehouse in SAP Yard Logistics
In this master data setup, you’ll use the SAP Fiori app Assign Docking
Location to Warehouse. To assign a docking location to a warehouse, for
each docking location, maintain the EWM Whno (warehouse number) field
and the EWM Business System field, as shown in Figure 7.7.
Figure 7.7 Assign Docking Location to Warehouse
3. Assign an external warehouse ID to a storage type in SAP Yard Logistics
In this master data setup, you’ll use the SAP Fiori app Assign External
Warehouse ID to Storage Type. To assign an external warehouse ID to a
storage type, maintain the EWM Warehouse ID, Yard No., and Storage Type
fields, as shown in Figure 7.8.
© 

431
Figure 7.8 Assign External Warehouse ID to Storage Type
4. Determine the SAP EWM door in SAP Yard Logistics
In this master data setup, you’ll use the SAP Fiori app Determine EWM Door.
To determine the SAP EWM door, link the EWM Dr/Ch (door or checkpoint)
to the Yard No. and Storage Bin, as shown in Figure 7.9.
Figure 7.9 Determine SAP EWM Door
5. Maintain logical ports for SAP EWM integration
In this master data setup, you’ll use the SAP Fiori app Maintain Logical Ports
for EWM Integration. To maintain logical ports for SAP EWM Integration,
assign Logical Ports for the EWM Business Systems, as shown in
Figure 7.10.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

432
Figure 7.10 Maintain Logical Ports for SAP EWM Integration
Process Demo
In this section, we’ll delve into the inbound process using SAP Yard Logistics and
SAP EWM:
1. Create a purchase order in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
To create a purchase order, execute Transaction ME21N. Maintain the
vendor, material group, purchase order quantity, plant, and storage
location and other mandatory required details to create the purchase order,
as shown in Figure 7.11. Note the purchase order number, which you’ll need
for the next step.
Figure 7.11 Create a Purchase Order
2. Create an inbound delivery with reference to a purchase order in SAP
ERP or SAP S/4HANA
To create an inbound delivery, execute Transaction VL31N. Enter supplier
and purchase order detail and other details as per the business process.
© 

433
Click Continue and then Save to generate an inbound delivery, as shown in
Figure 7.12. Note the inbound delivery number, which you’ll need for the
next step.
Figure 7.12 Create Inbound Delivery
3. Display the inbound delivery in SAP EWM
To display the inbound delivery, execute Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. In the
Find field, select Logistics Execution Delivery, and enter the delivery
number from earlier. Click Continue to display the inbound delivery, as
shown in Figure 7.13.
Figure 7.13 Display Inbound Delivery
4. Create a shipment in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
To create a shipment, execute Transaction VT01N. Enter the Transportation
Planning Point, Shipment Type and Packing Material and click Continue.
Then, assign the inbound delivery, click the Pack button, enter a packaging
continue. Click Continue and pack the shipment with pack material. Finally.
Click Save to generate shipment document. Note the shipment number, as
shown in Figure 7.14.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

434
Figure 7.14 Create Shipment
5. Display the shipment output in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
Staying on the shipment screen, note that separate shipment output types
are triggered for SAP EWM and SAP Yard Logistics. In the menu bar of the
shipment document, select Goto • Output to display the output types, as
shown in Figure 7.15.
Figure 7.15 Display Shipment Output
6. Display the TU in SAP EWM
The TU is automatically created in SAP EWM based on the shipment output
from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. To display the TU, execute Transaction
/SCWM/TU. Select EXT Transportation Unit. Enter the shipment number
created earlier and click Continue to generate an inbound delivery, as
shown in Figure 7.16.
Figure 7.16 Display TU
© 

435
7. Display the yard request in SAP Yard Logistics
A yard request is automatically created in SAP EWM based on the shipment
output from SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA. To display the yard request, execute
Transaction /UI2/FLP. Go to the Planning and Execution group and then
open the Monitor Yard Requests app. In the Reference Value field, enter the
delivery number and click Continue to show the yard request. Then, click
the Release button, as shown in Figure 7.17.
Figure 7.17 Display Yard Request
8. Display door assignment in SAP EWM
Perhaps, your warehouse receiving team should manually assign a door to
the TU in SAP EWM. To assign the TU, execute Transaction /SCWM/TU and
select the EXT Transportation Unit field. Enter the shipment number
created earlier and click Continue. Next, click the Assigned Doors tab, add
the door, and click Continue to show the door assignment, as shown in
Figure 7.18.
Figure 7.18 Door Assignment in SAP EWM
9. Display the yard order in SAP Yard Logistics
In SAP Yard Logistics, a yard clerk releases the yard request, which results in
creation of yard order. To display the yard order, execute Transaction
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

436
/UI2/FLP. Go to the Monitor Yard Orders app. In the Reference Value field,
enter the delivery number and click Continue to show the yard order. Click
the yard order number to display the yard order, as shown in Figure 7.19.
Figure 7.19 Display Yard Order
10. Trigger truck check-in in SAP Yard Logistics
The yard clerk manually triggers the check-in process for the truck in the
yard order in SAP Yard Logistics, as shown in Figure 7.20.
Figure 7.20 SAP Yard Logistics: Truck Check-In
11. Trigger truck check-in in SAP EWM
The S & R Activity of the TU is updated to Active when TU arrives at the
checkpoint in SAP EWM. Upon check-in in SAP Yard Logistics, the TU
becomes Active in SAP EWM, as shown in Figure 7.21.
Figure 7.21 SAP EWM: Truck Check-In
© 

437
12. Trigger truck check-in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
In SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the shipment automatically is updated with
the status 2 Check-in. To display the shipment, execute Transaction VT03N.
Next, enter the shipment number in Shipment field and click Continue, as
shown in Figure 7.22.
Figure 7.22 Truck Check-In in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
13. Door yard task confirmation in SAP Yard Logistics
In SAP Yard Logistics, the yard clerk confirms the yard task, which results in
the TU moving to the door, as shown in Figure 7.23.
Figure 7.23 Door Yard Task Confirmation
14. TU arrival at door in SAP EWM
The S & R Activity of the door is updated to Active as the TU arrives at the
door in SAP EWM, as shown in Figure 7.24.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

438
Figure 7.24 TU Arrival
15. Process the unloading of goods in SAP EWM
In SAP EWM, the warehouse unloading team completes the TU unloading
operation. In Transaction /SCWM/TU via the menu bar, select Action. Click
Start Unloading and Finish Unloading, as shown in Figure 7.25.
Figure 7.25 Process Unloading the Goods
16. Shipment unloading status update in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
In SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the shipment automatically is updated with
the status 4 Loading end. In Transaction VT03N, the unloading status is
updated, as shown in Figure 7.26.
Figure 7.26 Shipment Unloading Status Update
© 

439
17. Goods receipt and putaway in SAP EWM
In SAP EWM, the receiving warehouse team completes the goods receipt
and putaway process, as shown in Figure 7.27.
Figure 7.27 Goods Receipt and Putaway
18. TU movement to checkpoint in SAP Yard Logistics
In SAP Yard Logistics, the yard clerk moves the TU to the outbound
checkpoint. To display the yard order, execute Transaction /UI2/FLP. Go to
the Monitor Yard Order app. Enter the yard order 344 in the yard order field
and select the yard task. Click Start and Confirm to move the TU to the
checkpoint, as shown in Figure 7.28.
Figure 7.28 TU Movement to Checkpoint
19. Departure of the TU from door in SAP EWM
The S & R Activity of the door is updated to Completed as the TU departs
from the door in SAP EWM, as shown in Figure 7.29.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

440
Figure 7.29 Departure of the TU from Door
20. TU check-out in SAP Yard Logistics
In SAP Yard Logistics, a yard clerk sets up the TU for check-out. To display
the yard order, execute Transaction /UI2/FLP. Go to the Monitor Yard Order
app. Enter the yard order 345 in the Yard Order field and click Check Out,
as shown in Figure 7.30.
Figure 7.30 TU Check-Out
21. TU check-out in SAP EWM
The S & R Activity of the TU is updated to Completed as the TU departs
from the warehouse premises in SAP EWM, as shown in Figure 7.31.
Figure 7.31 TU Check-Out
22. Shipment completion in SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA
In SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA, the shipment automatically is updated with
the status as 7 Shipment end. In Transaction VT03N, enter the shipment
© 

441
number in the shipment number field and click Continue to check these
details, as shown in Figure 7.32.
Figure 7.32 Shipment Completion
Note
The inbound goods receipt process using SAP EWM, SAP Yard Logistics, and
SAP ERP or SAP S/4HANA is now complete.
7.2.2 Outbound Process
An outbound scenario with SAP Yard Logistics typically involves managing the
movement of goods or materials from a warehouse or distribution center to the
outbound transportation area, such as a trucking terminal or a loading dock.
Yard logistics play a crucial role in ensuring efficient and streamlined operations
during the outbound process. We’ll look at the outbound process in detail in the
following sections.
Business Process
As shown in Figure 7.33, the outbound goods issue process using SAP Yard
Logistics involves the following steps:
1. The first step in this process is to create a sales order for a customer in the
ERP or SAP S/4HANA system. The sales order is then converted into an
outbound delivery, which is automatically sent to SAP EWM for warehouse
processing.
2. Once the planning is complete, the shipment is distributed to both SAP
EWM and SAP Yard Logistics to initiate the process of truck arrival, loading,
and departure.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

442
3. The ERP message triggers the creation of the Yard Request document,
which is used to plan the first yard activity. This message is also sent to
SAP EWM, where a TU document is created containing information about
the planned content. Additionally, automatic door determination or
manual door assignment takes place, allowing SAP EWM to start the
picking and staging process.
4. It’s important to note that since SAP Yard Logistics and SAP EWM are
involved in this process, yard activities such as check-in posting or
movements should not be executed. These steps fall under the scope of
SAP Yard Logistics.
5. While the warehouse begins its activities in the yard, the Yard Order is
created based on the Yard Request. This document is used for processing
in the yard, and since this is an outbound scenario, an outbound Yard
Order is created. For the arrival of the truck, an inbound yard order is
required, which can be generated from the outbound Yard Order.
6. Meanwhile, in SAP EWM, outbound processes are occurring, and the
products are being staged. Simultaneously, various yard activities are
taking place in SAP Yard Logistics. Once the movement to the door is
activated, another door determination may occur, either when no door
determination has been triggered before or to validate the previously
determined door.
7. With the confirmation of the TU in SAP Yard Logistics, the arrival at the
door is posted in SAP EWM. At this point, the TU cannot be moved in the
yard any longer, and yard activities are only possible again after receiving
notification from SAP EWM that loading is complete.
8. This notification triggers yard activities, and the movement from the door
to the next yard location, such as the checkpoint for departure, can be
executed. A departure from door message is sent from SAP Yard Logistics
to SAP EWM.
9. Goods issue may be triggered in SAP EWM during this process, and the
latest possible point for the goods issue posting is the checkout of the TU.
After the loading notification is sent to SAP Yard Logistics, no further yard
activities are allowed in SAP EWM, and all postings occur in the yard.
10. Now that the truck has reached the outbound checkpoint, the check-out
can be posted, which is also sent to SAP EWM and triggers the check-out
© 

443
posting there. The ERP documents will be updated from SAP EWM based
on the goods issue and check-out posting.
Figure 7.33 Outbound Scenario with SAP Yard Logistics
Configuration
Let’s walk through step by step the configuration needs for an outbound process
using SAP Yard Logistics:
1. Assign SAP EWM business systems and warehouses to yards in SAP Yard
Logistics
This configuration setting is required to integrate SAP Yard Logistics with
SAP EWM. Follow the IMG menu path Yard Logistics • Integration •
Integration to SAP Extended Warehouse Management • Assign EWM
Business Systems and Warehouses to Yard, as shown in Figure 7.34.
Figure 7.34 Assign SAP EWM Business Systems and Warehouses to Yards
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

444
2. Maintain SAP EWM checkpoints in SAP Yard Logistics
This configuration setting is to maintain checkpoints. Follow the IMG menu
path Yard Logistics • Integration • Integration to SAP Extended
Warehouse Management • Maintain EWM Checkpoints, as shown in
Figure 7.35.
Figure 7.35 Maintain SAP EWM Checkpoints
Master Data Setup
Let’s now turn to the master data requirements for an outbound process using
SAP Yard Logistics:
1. Link Between Packaging Material (TU) and Means of Transport in SAP
Yard Logistics
In this master data setup, you’ll use the SAP Fiori app Link Between
Packaging Material (TU) and Means of Transport. To link packaging material
(TU) and means of transport, maintain the MTr (means of transport) and
Packaging Material fields, as shown in Figure 7.36.
© 

445
Figure 7.36 Link between Packaging Material (TU) and Means of Transport
2. Assign a docking location to a warehouse in SAP Yard Logistics
In this master data setup, you’ll use the SAP Fiori app Assign Docking
Location to Warehouse. To assign a docking location to a warehouse,
maintain the Docking Location, EWM Whno (warehouse number), and
EWM Business System fields, as shown in Figure 7.37.
Figure 7.37 Assign Docking Location to Warehouse
3. Assign an external warehouse ID to a storage type in SAP Yard Logistics
In this master data setup, you’ll use the SAP Fiori app Assign External
Warehouse ID to Storage Type. To assign external warehouse ID to storage
type, assign the EWM Warehouse ID to the Yard No and Storage Type, as
shown in Figure 7.38.
Personal Copy for peerly kazes, peerlyka@example.com

446
Figure 7.38 Assign External Warehouse ID to Storage Type

8 Environmental Health and Safety
The SAP Environment, Health, and Safety Management (SAP EHS
Management) module represents an all-encompassing system meticulously
crafted to effectively govern and oversee environmental health and safety
(EHS) risks within an organization. This module empowers enterprises to
diligently trace and ascertain compliance with regulatory requisites,
proactively identify and mitigate workplace hazards, and instill a culture
ingrained with safety consciousness among employees. Encompassing
myriad aspects such as incident management, risk assessment, safety
training, emergency response planning, and compliance reporting, the SAP
EHS Management module emerges as a robust framework to uphold the
highest standards of health and safety. The primary objective of this
chapter is to explicate the intricacies of the SAP EHS Management repertoire
—and its seamless integration with SAP Extended Warehouse Management
(SAP EWM) through the embedded Extended Warehouse Management in
SAP S/4HANA (embedded EWM) framework.
This SAP component offers comprehensive support for all activities pertaining to
product safety and stewardship. If your organization manufactures and sells
substances that are potentially harmful, it is of utmost importance to safeguard
human beings and the environment from the risks associated with these
substances. Additionally, you must comply with numerous laws and regulations
concerning hazardous substances on a global scale. This SAP component aids in
the secure handling of hazardous substances, ensuring their safe introduction to
the market and automating compliance with all relevant regulations.
SAP EHS Management and SAP EWM are distinct modules within an SAP system.
The integration of these two modules facilitates a more efficient and
streamlined management of hazardous materials and related processes.

emphasizes the key functionalities of SAP EHS Management. We subsequently
focus on the various options available for an inbound process using SAP EHS
Management, encompassing business processes, configuration, master data,
